title: Confirm additive-column policy
description:
Objective / why
Keep schema evolution narrow and auditable.

Exact scope
Allow only nullable/no-default additions outside active backfill; all other changes block or require fresh generation/reseed.

Traceability only (non-normative)
- docs/PLAN.md: §19 Decision register and M0 hard gate; §16 M0
- Requirements traceability is retained, but closure uses the embedded contract below.

Dependencies
- boring-cdc-d-ddl
- boring-cdc-d-values

## Rationale
Keep schema evolution narrow and auditable. The choice must be explicit at M0 because deferring it would force implementation agents to guess at a correctness, durability, security, interoperability, or public-claim boundary.

## Alternatives Considered
- Proposed/default boundary: Allow only nullable/no-default additions outside active backfill; all other changes block or require fresh generation/reseed.
- Defer the choice to implementation: rejected because docs/PLAN.md §19 makes it a blocking M0 decision.
- Widen the system beyond docs/PLAN.md §18: rejected as outside v0.1.

## Embedded decision scope
Freeze sole compatible nullable/non-generated/no-default addition outside active backfill, absent_for_schema-to-null projection, fingerprint transition, changed-Relation synchronous handling, active-generation invalidation, destination block/fresh generation outcomes.

## Validation tooling prerequisite
Consumes schemas and validator CLIs from `boring-cdc-m0.1` and `boring-cdc-m0.2`; this Bead owns its decision/artifact/domain content, never the shared validator implementation.
design:
Implementation / decision notes
Bind snapshots to immutable relation fingerprints and define destination projections.

Preserve these global invariants: one PostgreSQL source, one publication, one pgoutput slot, one Rust binary, one SQLite journal, ClickHouse plus one JSONL/Parquet archive; durable-before-feedback; destination-independent capture; at-least-once/idempotent convergence; explicit bounded failure; no comparison of source versions across capture epochs.

## Self-contained decision and fixture specification
Before closure record: accountable approver and dated source; selected literal value(s), versions/digests/units; exact contract artifact path and SHA-256; stable fixture IDs; supported matrix and fixed seeds; inputs/preconditions; deterministic fault hook/phase; expected state, exit, checkpoint/feedback/external effect, metrics and stable log/status codes; later executor Bead IDs; script path; result JSON schema and artifact root; redaction assertions. Runtime pass results are not required in M0, but the fixture must be mechanically executable and before closure this decision authors its own schema-valid row in `contracts/m0/decisions.json`, and every executor/fixture ID in that row must resolve. PLAN links are traceability only.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria
M0 closure requires the accountable owner to approve the exact boundary in this decision, plus a checked-in mechanically usable fixture specification that names inputs, expected outcomes/failures, artifact schema, and supported matrix. Runtime results are explicitly not required for M0. Later execution and result evidence are owned by: `boring-cdc-m1-ddl-fixtures`, `boring-cdc-m4-schema`.

## Decision closure validator
`scripts/validate/m0_decision.sh <bead-id>` rejects missing approvals, unresolved values, absent artifact hashes, nonexistent fixture/executor IDs, unowned expected transitions, missing log/redaction requirements, or downstream runtime results used as an M0 prerequisite. It writes `artifacts/m0/decisions/<bead-id>/evidence.json`; the later executor consumes the fixture ID without re-deciding it.
notes:
Explicit non-goals
No generic DDL migration or online table-set expansion.

Do not widen docs/PLAN.md section 18. Do not silently weaken a blocked/require-reseed outcome into best-effort continuation.

## Plan-space completeness rule
`contracts/coverage/plan-to-beads.json` assigns stable IDs for every invariant, configuration group, CLI command, state transition, test-matrix row, release criterion and risk/mitigation to exactly one canonical executing Bead with the full assertion embedded there. Consumers record owner Bead + evidence digest only. `scripts/validate/plan_coverage.sh` rejects missing/duplicate owners, future-evidence closure dependencies, PLAN-only normative references and unmapped commands/states/tests/risks. No feature may be removed to satisfy the validator.

title: Freeze archive durability and continuity contract
description:
Objective / why
Prevent partial or ambiguous archive publication after crashes.

Exact scope
Name supported Linux filesystems, directory rename/fsync rules, SEGMENT_READY, generation pointer, same-account reader model, writer versions, and reproducibility rules.

Traceability only (non-normative)

Dependencies

## Rationale
Prevent partial or ambiguous archive publication after crashes. The choice must be explicit at M0 because deferring it would force implementation agents to guess at a correctness, durability, security, interoperability, or public-claim boundary.

## Alternatives Considered

- Defer the choice to implementation: rejected because docs/PLAN.md §19 makes it a blocking M0 decision.
- Widen the system beyond docs/PLAN.md §18: rejected as outside v0.1.

## Retained archive audit contract
Freeze read-only selector/manifest/`SEGMENT_READY`/file-hash audit, separate persisted journal/self-consistency cursors and ranges, per-pass byte/event/time budgets, cadence/freshness windows, gaps/unverifiable boundary, and mismatch recovery.

## Shared destination failure decision
Freeze the identical cross-destination taxonomy: transient environmental failures persist capped exponential backoff/jitter and a retry budget across restart; deterministic poison/configuration/contract/integrity failures or exhausted budgets block without hot-loop or checkpoint skip; explicit resume revalidates the corrected cause and unchanged failed boundary.

## Embedded decision scope
Freeze filesystem allowlist/mount assumptions, opaque ASCII path grammar, 0700/0600 owner/link/type rules, descriptor-relative no-follow/exclusive calls, every write/fsync/rename/ready/checkpoint hook, deterministic writer pins, greatest-fence selector, journal/self-consistency cursors and budgets, FailurePolicy classes, logs and recovery. Destination-neutral promotion is owned by d-promotion.

## Validation tooling prerequisite
Consumes schemas and validator CLIs from `boring-cdc-m0.1` and `boring-cdc-m0.2`; this Bead owns its decision/artifact/domain content, never the shared validator implementation.

## Shared failure-policy dependency
Consume the immutable enum, persisted schedule, fingerprint, transition, and re-arm contract from `boring-cdc-d-failure-policy`. This decision owns only its domain-specific failure mapping and recovery hook; it must not redefine retry classes, schedule literals, or attempt persistence.

## Approved robustness revision ownership
Freeze finite archive audit rounds with complete target checkpoint, epoch/generation/selector/contract identity, renewed passes over promised freshness, and unit-fit or bounded resume. m5-segment-set solely executes domain audit rounds; m2-schema owns persistence and m5-loops schedules domain APIs.

title: Freeze the shared failure and retry policy
description:
Objective / why
Prevent capture, ClickHouse, and archive from independently inventing retry classes, persisted schedules, poison behavior, or re-arm rules.

Exact decision
Approve one versioned typed `FailurePolicy` contract shared by all three domains. It owns the exhaustive failure-class enum; stable redacted fingerprint inputs; persisted attempt/schedule fields; capped exponential backoff and deterministic jitter literals; restart semantics; failed-boundary identity; same-fingerprint suppression; transition rules for transient, deterministic, integrity, continuity, configuration, resource-pressure, and operator-blocked failures; and the common re-arm token/result shape. Domain Beads supply only typed recovery hooks and domain-specific safe states. Unlimited supervised process restarts do not erase or bypass the persisted attempt schedule. No class permits checkpoint/feedback skip, silent drop, hot-loop, or cross-epoch retry.

## Rationale
One shared state machine makes retry behavior reviewable, persistent, and identical at the safety boundary while typed hooks preserve domain-specific recovery.

## Alternatives Considered
- Per-domain retry loops: rejected because class, schedule, persistence, and re-arm semantics drift.
- A dynamic policy language/plugin framework: rejected as unnecessary v0.1 scope and harder to exhaustively test.
- Process-local retry state: rejected because supervised restart would reset attempts and hot-loop.

Inputs and outputs
Author the sole schema-valid decision row and immutable `contracts/m0/failure-policy.json` containing policy/schema version, enum and exhaustive match requirements, schedule literals and units, fingerprint canonicalization/redaction rules, persisted fields, transition table, allowed re-arm predicates, status/metric/log codes, executor/fixture IDs, and SHA-256 digest. `boring-cdc-m2.1` owns the shared Rust type/persistence-adapter/scheduler implementation; capture and destination handlers consume it through typed hooks.

Dependencies
- boring-cdc-m0.1
- boring-cdc-m0.2

Non-goals
No generic connector framework, dynamic policy language, arbitrary user callbacks, distributed scheduler, automatic data skipping, or weakening of domain continuity rules.

## Approved robustness revision ownership
Specify expected deterministic safe-stop close separately from unexpected CopyBoth loss. m2.1 retains policy/fingerprint ownership; m2-ownership supplies generation-bound lifecycle interface; m2-capture-runtime owns real persist-before-close and no-reconnect behavior.
design:
## Implementation notes
Use a closed Rust enum and one pure transition function over persisted state, time input, deterministic jitter seed, relevant configuration fingerprint, failed boundary, and typed domain outcome. Fingerprints include stable error code and canonical nonsecret context, never payloads, keys, DSNs, raw driver strings, tokens, source identifiers, or absolute paths. Policy configuration is versioned and fingerprinted; a changed unrelated setting cannot re-arm a failure. Capture may project deterministic failure to `capture_safe_stopped`; destination workers project it to their own blocked state, but both retain the same policy record and checkpoint boundary.

Specification evidence
Provide mechanically usable golden vectors for every class/transition, near/at/over schedule bound, attempt persistence across restart, clock movement, deterministic jitter, same/different fingerprint, relevant/unrelated config change, explicit operator re-arm, stale completion, and domain-hook output. Include negative vectors proving no feedback/checkpoint advance, no attempt reset on process restart, no payload/secret in fingerprint/log, and no retry after integrity/continuity failure without its stronger recovery. Runtime execution is downstream, not required for M0 closure.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria
The accountable implementation lead approves every literal, field, enum member, transition, status/log/metric code, and domain hook. `scripts/validate/m0_decision.sh boring-cdc-d-failure-policy` validates the row/artifact, exhaustive golden corpus, stable digest, owner, and later core executor `boring-cdc-m2.1` plus real-adapter executors `boring-cdc-m2-capture-runtime`, `boring-cdc-m2-jsonl`, `boring-cdc-m4-durability` and `boring-cdc-m5-loops`. The PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, and archive decision Beads reference this exact artifact digest and contain no second retry taxonomy or schedule. M0 closure requires specification/fixture approval only, never downstream runtime results.

## Approved robustness revision acceptance
Approve expected close/delayed EOF/unmatched EOF/persistence failure/advisory-loss race vectors. A close token never suppresses loss on another generation or advisory session, nor authorizes in-process reconnect. Execute actual transport proofs later in m2-capture-runtime.
notes: Standalone canonical policy decision. PLAN references are traceability only. This preserves destination independence and domain-specific recovery while removing duplicated classification/scheduling ownership.

Inputs are Beads JSON, fixture specifications, executor IDs, approvals, artifact hashes, coverage rows, log/evidence manifests, and graph exports. Outputs are stable machine-readable diagnostics and nonzero exit on missing/duplicate owners, unresolved literals, nonexistent fixture/executor IDs, future-evidence prerequisites, absent hashes, malformed correlation fields, unredacted secrets, incomplete cleanup, or PLAN-only normative dependencies. The common evidence schema requires both `evidence_profile` and `evidence_tier`. Profile is `runtime`, `external_managed`, or `documentation`; tier is `leaf`, `component`, `milestone`, or `release`. Profile determines the kind of evidence; tier determines its cost and closure boundary.

- `leaf`: targeted format/lint/schema plus Bead-owned unit/property/contract/golden checks; no unrelated workspace-wide suite, Compose environment, fault matrix, or mandatory second full run.
- `component`: targeted checks plus the owning external-boundary e2e/fault suite and its deterministic rerun.
- `milestone`: workspace/all-target checks, milestone integration/fault suite, clean-environment reproducibility, and aggregate exit assertions.
- `release`: M6 endurance/full matrix and M7 clean-clone release reproduction.

Any generic test/e2e/fault/double-run prose in an effective contract is conditional on this normative tier; a task-specific tier section wins where old copied boilerplate conflicts. Runtime profiles require exactly the checks selected by tier. External-managed requires deterministic local baseline, provider-access provenance, exact attempted scenarios, sanitized provider outputs, and explicit unavailable/unsupported outcomes without fabricated hooks. Documentation requires schema/link/example/clean-clone walkthrough tests and records `fault_not_applicable` with justification; it may not claim runtime evidence.

Require upstream implementation of `scripts/validate/beads_snapshot.sh` and the canonical normalized graph schema. Gate scripts consume one captured snapshot digest for their entire run. Gate tooling uses only `br`: `br sync --witness --json` hashes the tracked JSONL without opening SQLite; an isolated `br sync --import-only` plus normalized export proves round-trip semantics; local pre-commit validation compares the ignored SQLite DB with JSONL before `br sync --flush-only`. ## Acceptance Criteria
The structured `acceptance_criteria` field is normative and must be satisfied in full; this heading exists so `br lint` and human readers find the contract consistently.

Every effective contract materializes the authority hierarchy and fail-closed conflict rule: a Bead cannot silently override REQUIREMENTS, approved contracts, canonical architecture ownership, or evidence provenance. The default 16 KiB limit applies to the generated summary body, excluding the separately attached full selected Bead, its manifest, and explicitly requested expansions. design:
Implementation contract
Keep validators deterministic, hermetic, path-safe, and independent of PostgreSQL/ClickHouse/runtime code. Parse JSON/JSONL without rewriting source files; reject duplicate keys/IDs and unknown schema versions. Resolve Bead/executor IDs against the exported graph, distinguish parent-child from blocking edges, and prove no M0 record requires an M1-M7 runtime result. The coverage validator requires exactly one canonical executing owner for every invariant, configuration clause, CLI command, persistent state/transition, §15 scenario, §17 criterion, and §20 risk; consumers may link evidence digests without re-owning transitions.

Unit and contract tests
A table-driven validator corpus covers valid minimal/full manifests plus malformed JSON, duplicate IDs/owners, missing executor, nonexistent script/fixture, forward evidence, unresolved/TBD literals, hash mismatch, path traversal/symlink attempt, unknown schema, nondeterministic ordering, secret corpus, missing correlation field, incomplete teardown, and stale/closed evidence. Golden diagnostics are byte-stable and contain no secret values.

Executable e2e/fault scripts
`scripts/e2e/m0_validation_tooling.sh` creates an isolated synthetic Beads graph and valid decision/artifact/coverage/evidence manifests, runs every validator twice, and compares byte-identical normalized output. `scripts/faults/m0_validation_tooling.sh` injects every invalid corpus case and asserts exact stable error code, JSON pointer, owning Bead, exit status, and no source mutation. Scripts run from a clean checkout, use fixed seed `m0-validator-v1`, avoid sleeps, capture exact commands/versions, and clean temporary state by trap.

Logging and evidence
Write redacted JSONL with `schema_version`, `case_event_seq`, `bead_id`, `scenario_id`, `correlation_id`, `component=m0_validation`, `phase`, `outcome`, validator version, fixture/executor ID, finding code, input/output digest, and artifact path relative to repository root. ## Incremental runbook registry contract
The schema supports `declared` rows before M6 and `complete` rows at M6. A condition-owning Bead authors its stable ID, version, condition/reason codes, owner, allowed-action interface, and procedure owner at its own closure; it never depends on future procedure evidence. `boring-cdc-m6-runbooks` later owns procedure bodies and aggregate promotion of all rows to `complete`. The validator rejects duplicate IDs, condition gaps, unknown actions/owners, incompatible version reuse, future-evidence closure, or a release with any row still declared.

## World-state, effective-contract, and projection contract
Consume the leaf-owned deterministic schemas for `world_state`, effective contracts, context packs, impact sets, claim indexes, and handoffs. One operation consumes one captured graph digest. Context packs declare included/omitted IDs, source digests, and byte/token estimate and fail with an expansion plan when complete normative content exceeds the bound. Effective contracts materialize versioned common policy plus task-specific deltas and make affected Beads stale after canonical changes. Evidence reuse defaults to exact digests; a wider compatibility predicate must name its owner and tests. This tooling validates and projects only—it never claims work, edits product state, commits, pushes, or creates a daemon.

design:
## Immutable claims and compatibility
Claims bind owner/scenario IDs to Git, graph, effective-contract, code/binary, fixture, image, config/profile, seed/environment, command/result/artifact/redaction digests and freshness or timeless applicability. Exact declared inputs must match; wider compatible ranges require a canonical owner and tested predicate. Report exact invalidating input and rerun owner. Historical evidence remains immutable and cannot prove changed semantics. No cached-success guessing.

## Findings and handoffs
Each append-only FINDING row separates verified observations from hypotheses, affected IDs, environment/input digests, failed approach, owner/status, resolution/invalidation trigger and supersession. No handoff promotes a hypothesis to normative contract. A handoff binds before/head/dirty world state, changes/IDs, completed/failed/stale checks, facts/observations/hypotheses, active/ambiguous intents, risks, unsafe repeats and exact next safe command; large logs are digest references. Redaction excludes secrets/raw payloads/DSNs/driver errors/absolute paths.

## Corpus
Valid/incompatible/exactly-compatible claims; missing/forged owners, unowned compatibility ranges, superseded evidence, time freshness, provenance gaps, rewritten history, cross-epoch/fixture/config/image mismatches; malformed finding/handoff, hypothesis promotion, ambiguous effects, unsafe-repeat omissions, hostile paths and secrets. Use supplied frozen world-state/effective-contract fixtures, not live decision or runtime results.

- boring-cdc-m1-ddl-fixtures

## Embedded canonical contract and unique ownership
Own pure bootstrap/restart/reseed state vectors: intent-before-slot, consistent-point/start_seq, exporter/importer/guard lifecycle, first-statement imports, feedback gate, lower stitch, fence, invalidation/release, retained-slot drain and full-reseed transitions; no M2 runtime evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria
The structured `acceptance_criteria` field below is normative and must be satisfied in full; this heading exists so tracker lint and human readers find the contract consistently.

## Embedded initial bootstrap specification
### 7.1 Initial bootstrap protocol

The permanent slot and its one-use creation snapshot are created only in the M3 bootstrap vertical slice, after M2 can durably store bootstrap state.

1. Initialize SQLite and validate/create the publication and connector-owned control relations; do not independently create and abandon the permanent slot snapshot.
2. Persist a `bootstrap_intent` in state `prepared` with a proposed capture epoch, slot/publication identity, table-set fingerprint, configuration fingerprint, and `exporter_liveness=not_started` **before** issuing slot creation.
3. On a dedicated read-only SQL connection that is forbidden from writing, creating temporary objects, or otherwise acquiring an XID, begin the DDL-guard transaction, acquire `ACCESS SHARE` locks on every selected relation in frozen canonical order, and verify the finite admitted relation contracts **before slot creation or snapshot export**. Hold this guard through durable observation of the post-copy capture fence. Every contract-changing DDL operation admitted by M0 must conflict with this guard; polling/fingerprint checks alone never admit DDL.
4. With the guard already held, `boring-cdc run --bootstrap` uses the dedicated capture/bootstrap role and connector guard to create only the configured permanent logical slot with `EXPORT_SNAPSHOT` on one dedicated replication exporter connection. This is permitted only while both ownership locks and the matching persisted intent from step 2 remain valid. The runtime then keeps that exact connection command-idle; it does not start `START_REPLICATION` on the exporter.
5. While that exact exporter connection is alive, atomically persist the returned slot `consistent_point` as both the snapshot boundary and a separate server-established creation-floor field, plus the exported snapshot identifier, source identity, and `start_seq`; then transition through `snapshot_exported` to `imports_pending`. `start_seq` is the current durable complete journal transaction boundary immediately before capture starts (the explicit zero-boundary sentinel in a fresh store). The pair `(consistent_point, start_seq)` is the initial anchor's lower stitch proof, but `consistent_point` is never represented as a decoded/durable source transaction. Persist all fields before any worker copies rows.
6. Start `START_REPLICATION` at the consistent point on a **separate** CopyBoth-capable replication connection only after that SQLite transaction commits. While that snapshot generation remains eligible, later journaled transactions are not feedback-eligible until every intended importer has durably acknowledged a successful snapshot import; atomic generation invalidation releases this gate as described below. A requested status reply may use the protocol zero sentinel or repeat the verified server creation floor, but the connector never proactively acknowledges that floor or advances through later WAL before the importer gate opens.
7. Each bounded importer begins a read-only `REPEATABLE READ` transaction and executes `SET TRANSACTION SNAPSHOT` as its first statement before any catalog or data query. It verifies the already guarded relation contracts through the imported snapshot. Worker import acknowledgements include assigned ranges and become durable only after import and contract binding succeed. The exporter, importer, and guard sessions use explicit admitted session timeouts; the guard issues a bounded read-only keepalive statement often enough to remain within those limits without hiding a failed probe.
8. Once every worker import acknowledgement is durable, transition to `imports_complete` and `exporter_release_permitted`; closing the command-idle exporter is then legitimate, not generation invalidation. Worker transactions remain alive until assigned reads finish; the independently acquired DDL guard remains alive through fence observation. Every chunk binds to the immutable `snapshot_schema_fingerprint` imported by its worker.
9. Snapshot rows use the persisted slot consistent point, `origin_rank=0`, and zero transaction/mutation ordinals. WAL uses its commit LSN and `origin_rank=1`, so WAL at an equal/later source position wins.
10. After all chunks are durably complete, create the published transactional fence described in section 7.3. Its observed and journaled source-transaction boundary is the sole `post_copy_fence_lsn` proof. Release the DDL guard only after the matching fence record is durably visible in SQLite.
11. An anchor becomes complete only after all snapshot chunks, all importer/schema acknowledgements, `(consistent_point, start_seq)`, and the matching durable fence record exist. Close exporter/importer/guard transactions at their explicit lifecycle points and report snapshot/XID/lock age throughout.

`bootstrap_intents` records monotonic states including `prepared`, `snapshot_exported`, `imports_pending`, `imports_complete`, `exporter_release_permitted`, `exporter_released`, `snapshot_unusable`, `bootstrap_ambiguous_requires_restart`, `existing_slot_generation_required`, and terminal anchor/re-seed states. It separately records exporter liveness and each worker import acknowledgement; a persisted token is not treated as a reusable snapshot after its exporter has died.

There is an unavoidable response/persistence crash window around remote slot creation. On restart, an intent with a now-existing slot but no persisted snapshot token transitions to `bootstrap_ambiguous_requires_restart`; the lost creation snapshot cannot be reconstructed. If the exporter is lost before every worker import acknowledgement, atomically invalidate that snapshot generation, make all of its snapshot events permanently non-promotable, and release its importer feedback gate. Once no usable snapshot basis is pending, journal durability is again the only feedback precondition, so capture can drain retained WAL rather than wait forever for acknowledgements that can no longer arrive. Do **not** drop an unused-but-WAL-retaining slot merely to obtain a later snapshot: transient insert/delete activity between snapshots would disappear from both baselines. Recovery first proves source identity, deterministic slot provenance, publication/protocol fingerprint, and uninterrupted WAL availability. When all are provable, start capture from the existing slot, durably drain its retained WAL into the journal, establish a locally durable lower stitch boundary, and run section 7.2's existing-slot snapshot protocol in the same capture epoch. If provenance or WAL continuity is ambiguous, create a new capture epoch and perform a confirmed full re-seed with an explicit continuity break. Deterministic crash hooks cover before slot creation, after server response, token persistence, every importer acknowledgement, exporter release, first feedback, and an insert-then-delete committed between the lost and replacement snapshots.

## Approved robustness revision ownership
Use the m1.1 bounded deterministic harness on this domain's production transition specification/functions; expose typed completion, clock and cancellation inputs.

Implementation / decision notes
Protocol/state-machine fixtures may use a test persistence harness; durable SQLite implementation is M2/M3.

Preserve these global invariants: one PostgreSQL source, one publication, one pgoutput slot, one Rust binary, one SQLite journal, ClickHouse plus one JSONL/Parquet archive; durable-before-feedback; destination-independent capture; at-least-once/idempotent convergence; explicit bounded failure; no comparison of source versions across capture epochs.

Bootstrap crash-state decision matrix
- No remote slot and no persisted successful response: retry the prepared creation intent.
- Remote slot exists but the creation snapshot token/consistent point was not durably persisted: transition to `bootstrap_ambiguous_requires_restart`; never attach silently and never drop/recreate merely to obtain another snapshot.
- Exporter dies before every worker has durably acknowledged importing the exact snapshot: invalidate that snapshot generation. The DDL guard is independent: prove it was acquired before export and remains held through durable fence observation; it does not import or acknowledge the snapshot.
- For a lost creation snapshot, first prove source identity, deterministic slot provenance, publication/protocol fingerprint, and uninterrupted availability of every required WAL record. When proved, retain the existing slot, start capture from it, durably drain retained WAL into the journal, establish a locally durable lower stitch boundary, and run the existing-slot snapshot protocol in the same capture epoch.
- Server feedback/confirmed-flush position is evidence in the continuity proof, not a standalone drop/recreate or re-seed decision rule. Any unavailable required WAL, provenance mismatch, or ambiguous continuity creates a new capture epoch and confirmed full re-seed with an explicit continuity break.
- After every worker import acknowledgement is durably read back, normal exporter release is legitimate. Worker copying and the independently held DDL guard continue through their documented lifecycle; guard loss before the durable capture fence invalidates the generation.
Every branch reconciles persisted intent, current slot identity/state, exporter liveness, token durability, worker import acknowledgements, DDL-guard acquisition/liveness, server positions, and retained-WAL continuity before mutation.

## Accepted review corrections
Specify pre-export guard acquisition and lost-snapshot retained-slot recovery versus new-epoch re-seed, including transient insert/delete and bounded backend cleanup.

## Creation-floor hardening
Store the server-established slot-creation consistent point separately from nullable durable transaction-end progress. Never fabricate a source transaction or proactively acknowledge the floor. While the snapshot generation remains eligible and importer acknowledgements are pending, requested replies may only use the pinned zero sentinel or verified floor and later WAL is not feedback-eligible. Atomic invalidation releases that gate; durable complete WAL can then drain while the snapshot rows remain non-promotable.

## Standalone implementation and evidence contract
Standalone execution contract
This Bead is sufficient for implementation and closure. PLAN/REQUIREMENTS links are navigation only. Preserve the fixed topology: one PostgreSQL source/database/publication/pgoutput slot, one Rust binary and SQLite journal, ClickHouse plus one scheduled JSONL/Parquet archive; durable-before-feedback; destination-independent capture; at-least-once delivery with idempotent convergence; bounded resources; fail-closed unsupported behavior; no cross-epoch version comparison. Values selected by M0 are copied as literals into this Bead or its produced contract before readiness; unresolved/TBD values block readiness.

Inputs, outputs, and ownership
Implement only this Bead's named domain transitions. Consume predecessor artifacts by immutable ID/digest; do not re-own their transitions. State changes use the capture-priority writer and complete SQLite transactions where applicable. External effects require an immutable intent, generation/epoch namespace, reconciliation, and checkpoint advancement only at complete journal transaction boundaries. Every failure names its class, stable fingerprint, failed boundary, allowed actions, and recovery.

Security and observability
Emit redacted JSONL with `schema_version`, monotonically increasing `case_event_seq`, `bead_id`, `scenario_id`, `correlation_id`, `run_id`, `capture_epoch`, `component`, `phase`, `outcome`, `config_fingerprint`, and as applicable `generation`, `intent_id`, `request_id`, XID, commit/end LSN, journal range, anchor/fence, attempt, fault hook, failure class/fingerprint, metric units, and evidence digest. JSON null is used for inapplicable fields. Never log payload values, canonical keys/tuples, snapshot tokens, DSNs, credentials, dry-run nonces, raw driver errors, secret environment names/values, raw source identifiers, or absolute/unapproved paths.

Deterministic evidence
Own comprehensive unit/contract tests for every branch, limit, invalid input, state transition, crash boundary, retry, and stale completion in this Bead. Required commands are `cargo test --locked --workspace --all-targets`, a Bead-specific test filter, `scripts/e2e/m1_bootstrap_sm.sh`, and `scripts/faults/m1_bootstrap_sm.sh`. Scripts run from a clean checkout, create isolated volumes/state with fixed seed/profile, build/start pinned Compose services, wait by health conditions rather than sleeps, execute named fault hooks, assert exact state/checkpoint/external effects and metrics, collect evidence, and tear down via a trap. Run twice to prove reproducibility.

Artifacts
Write `artifacts/boring-cdc-m1-bootstrap-sm/<scenario_id>/<seed>/` containing `manifest.json`, `commands.txt`, `versions.json`, redacted `config.json`, `logs/boring-cdc.jsonl`, `state/before.json`, `state/after.json`, `fault-timeline.json`, oracle/packet evidence when applicable, stdout/stderr, and SHA-256 inventory. `manifest.json` records schema version, Bead/case, git and binary hashes, image digests, seed/profile, exact commands/exit codes, configuration and source/table fingerprints, assertions, artifact hashes, outcome, and failure fingerprint. Closure records artifact paths/digests and proves log-schema/redaction checks pass.

title: Implement the shared CLI command, output, and exit-code contract
description:
Objective / why
Give users one predictable command surface before milestone-specific handlers are implemented: discoverable help, stable automation output, safe confirmations, actionable errors, and no secret leakage.

Exact scope
Own the canonical command registry and parser shell, global flags, versioned text/JSON result and error envelopes, stdout/stderr rules, stable exit-code taxonomy, shell-safe rendered confirmations, and command-help compatibility snapshots. Domain Beads own handler behavior and state transitions; this Bead does not open SQLite writable, contact PostgreSQL/ClickHouse, or implement a generic plugin framework.

Dependencies
- boring-cdc-m0-gate
- boring-cdc-m1-config

## Embedded complete public command inventory
### 12.1 Commands

```text
boring-cdc check
boring-cdc init
boring-cdc run
boring-cdc run --bootstrap
boring-cdc status [--json]

boring-cdc backfill start|pause|resume|status
boring-cdc backfill restart --confirm

boring-cdc destination list|add|pause|resume
boring-cdc destination add NEW_DESTINATION --archive-root PATH --continuity-break --from-seq SEQ --dry-run
boring-cdc destination add NEW_DESTINATION --archive-root PATH --continuity-break --from-seq SEQ --confirm-data-gap
boring-cdc destination detach --confirm
boring-cdc destination promote DESTINATION --generation ID --confirm
boring-cdc destination retire DESTINATION --generation ID --confirm
boring-cdc destination verify DESTINATION [--from-seq SEQ] [--json]
boring-cdc archive reconstruct DESTINATION --selector-fence FENCE --output PATH
boring-cdc archive verify DESTINATION --selector-fence FENCE --oracle-manifest PATH [--json]

boring-cdc replay DESTINATION --from-anchor/--from-seq/--since --new-generation ID --dry-run
boring-cdc replay DESTINATION --from-anchor/--from-seq/--since --new-generation ID --confirm-replay
boring-cdc journal inspect [--event-id ID --explain] [--json]
boring-cdc journal verify
boring-cdc journal gc --dry-run

boring-cdc recover inspect
boring-cdc recover promotion DESTINATION --adopt-external-fence --confirm
boring-cdc recover reseed --recreate-publication --recreate-slot --confirm-data-gap
boring-cdc recover reseed --add-table SCHEMA.TABLE --recreate-publication --recreate-slot --confirm-data-gap
boring-cdc recover reseed --resume RESEED_ID --confirm
```

`init` initializes local state and publication/control relations; it does not create and abandon the permanent slot's one-time exported snapshot. `run --bootstrap` owns initial slot/snapshot lifecycle after persisting its intent. Direct live `ALTER PUBLICATION` is unsupported and continuity-breaking. Selecting a new table is expressed only as a confirmed full re-seed/new epoch.

Mutating commands first provide a dry-run showing the current source identity, `run_id`, capture epoch, configuration/table-set fingerprint, anchor/generation, intended transitions, retained-history requirements, source/destination consequences, expected interruption, and rollback/recovery path. Text output includes one shell-escaped, copy-pasteable confirmation command; JSON output includes the same canonical arguments plus an opaque short-lived `confirm_token`. The operator never computes a hash or reconstructs hidden arguments. The token binds the nonce, request ID, canonical payload digest, and expiry, is accepted only for that exact displayed transition, and is redacted from logs/artifacts. The lock-owning runtime issues a fresh unpredictable per-dry-run nonce; destructive confirmation uses `hash(nonce || canonical_request_payload)`, whose payload includes the displayed fingerprints and short expiry, and cannot authorize a changed source/epoch/configuration/table set/generation. A new dry-run always receives a new nonce, while retrying the exact displayed dry-run reuses its request ID. Replay of an established destination always targets a named new generation, requires `--confirm-replay` after dry-run, and needs a separate verified promotion; it cannot rewrite the live checkpoint.

While `run` is active, every routine mutating command is an authenticated local request to its Unix-domain owner endpoint; the CLI never opens SQLite writable. The request ID is `hash(nonce || canonical_request_payload)` and is persisted with that payload hash before the transition; retrying that exact dry-run after a lost reply reuses the ID, while a new issuance cannot collide. The terminal result is persisted before reply, and a lost reply is recovered by resubmitting that same request. Same-ID/different-payload, expired digest, peer mismatch, stale `run_id`, or changed fingerprint fails closed. Startup marks every nonterminal prior-run request `aborted_by_restart` after reconciling any remote intent and never re-executes it automatically. Only `backfill pause`, `destination pause`, and `destination detach` after bound confirmation are routine offline-eligible commands; they acquire both ownership locks, wait/reconcile under the takeover rule, persist the same request/intent record, and leave long-running work for the next `run`. Backfill start/resume/restart, destination add/resume/promote, and replay require a live owner endpoint. Source administration remains maintenance-only. The status/Prometheus listener is read-only under every configuration.

`init`, `destination retire ... --confirm`, `recover promotion ... --adopt-external-fence`, and source-mutating recovery/re-seed commands are maintenance-runtime commands under section 3. Retirement revalidates the greatest selector, grace, absence of leases/pins, and exact generation before loading the ClickHouse maintenance role to delete only that retired generation's partition/data. Promotion recovery reads the externally greatest valid selector, proves it names an existing internally consistent generation, persists `highest_external_fence` plus an adoption record in `destination_promotion_intents`, and permits only a subsequent fence strictly greater than the adopted value. It never changes the external live generation as part of adoption. They refuse to run while ordinary `run` holds either lock. After a clean handoff they become the sole owner, observe the stale-ownership wait, and reconcile local/source/external intents. Only that maintenance owner may load the administration DSN, and only around the exact owner-only request and verification. Read-only commands such as `check` and `status` do not take ownership or load administration credentials. `destination verify` is a nonce-free idempotent request asking the live owner to run its bounded audit now, persist the result through the capture-priority writer, and return that persisted record; it never advances a checkpoint. With no live owner it opens local state and the destination read-only, prints an explicitly `offline_diagnostic_not_persisted` result, and cannot block/unblock a destination or claim durable audit freshness.

## Stable result contract
Every command supports `-h/--help`; every status/list/inspect/check/verify/dry-run operation supports `--json`. JSON uses `schema_version`, `command`, `outcome`, stable `code`, human `message`, nullable `request_id`, `run_id`, `capture_epoch`, `condition`, `runbook_id`, `data`, `warnings`, and safe `next_commands`. Text sends primary data to stdout and diagnostics to stderr. Exit codes are frozen as: `0` success; `2` invocation/configuration invalid; `3` safety/continuity blocked with operator action; `4` transient dependency unavailable; `5` integrity/corruption or unverifiable state; `6` internal invariant failure. Unknown future codes are nonzero and JSON-versioned.

## Confirmation UX
Dry-runs return one shell-escaped copy-paste command in text and canonical argv plus opaque short-lived `confirm_token` in JSON. Users never compute hashes. Token/request/nonce values are redacted from logs and artifacts; stale, changed, cross-source, cross-run, and replayed tokens fail with stable codes.

## Offline confirmation boundary
The CLI renderer/parser never persists an offline nonce itself. It invokes the short-lived dual-lock issuance/confirmation transactions owned by `boring-cdc-m2-ownership`, renders only their canonical result, and treats owner/race/stale outcomes through the stable envelope.

## Acceptance Criteria
The structured `acceptance_criteria` field is normative and must be satisfied in full; this heading exists so `br lint` and human readers find the contract consistently.

## Canonical runtime snapshot and action-plan envelopes
Own versioned shared `SystemSnapshot` and `ActionPlan` JSON envelopes. `SystemSnapshot` carries snapshot/state revision, freshness, source/capture/run/ownership identity, fingerprints, durability boundaries, budgets, destination/audit state, conditions/runbooks, blockers, allowed actions, next-command templates, and evidence digest. `ActionPlan` records observation snapshot/revision provenance and binds one mutating dry-run to action-relevant control revisions and records preconditions, intended transitions/effects, resource/continuity consequences, rollback boundary, expected postconditions, confirmation policy, and plan digest. Domain Beads populate and own domain fields/transitions.


## Approved robustness revision ownership
Own ActionPlan control-revision dependency schema, current predicate list and observation provenance; register journal inspect --explain as a distinct operation variant owned solely by m5.1, while base journal inspection stays m2-reconcile. Freeze forecast/attestation/explanation result shapes with synthetic domain facts; real integration belongs to later owners.
design:
Use one typed `CommandSpec` registry and one typed `CliResult`/`CliError` envelope consumed by every command owner. Handler registration must name owning Bead, mutation/read-only class, live/offline/maintenance ownership requirement, confirmation policy, JSON support, exit-code set, runbook IDs, and redaction policy. Generate help/command inventory and compatibility fixtures from that registry; do not scatter clap subcommand definitions or ad-hoc exit calls across modules.

Unit tests
Table-driven tests cover every command/alias/required argument/global flag, help traversal, stdout/stderr separation, JSON schema versions, exit-code mapping, Unicode/quoted/path arguments, shell escaping, broken pipe, TTY/non-TTY, color disabled in machine output, token redaction, and unknown handler/result invariants. Snapshot tests fail on undocumented command or output-schema drift.

E2E/fault scripts and logging
`scripts/e2e/m1_cli_contract.sh` executes every help and parse-only success path from a clean checkout with fixed seed `cli-contract-v1`, validates text and JSON against goldens, and proves no source/store mutation. `scripts/faults/m1_cli_contract.sh` exercises every invalid/stale/redaction/path/pipe case and exact exit code. Emit redacted JSONL with schema/case sequence, bead/scenario/correlation, command and owner Bead, phase/outcome/code, JSON schema, TTY mode, and evidence digest—never argv values marked secret, tokens/nonces, DSNs, payloads, raw paths, or raw driver errors. Run twice, trap cleanup, and write manifest/commands/versions/logs/stdout/stderr/golden diffs/SHA-256 inventory under `artifacts/boring-cdc-m1-cli-contract/<scenario>/cli-contract-v1/`.

## Inspect-plan-apply-verify compatibility
Generate command help, handler ownership, snapshot/action schemas, and compatibility goldens from one typed registry. A confirmation is valid only for the exact action-plan digest and unchanged bound state/fingerprints. Terminal results cite the plan and postcondition-evidence digests. The envelopes are projections and do not create an independent runtime state machine.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance Criteria
The registry contains every embedded command exactly once with a resolvable owner Bead and correct read-only/live/offline/maintenance/confirmation classification. `cargo test --locked --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo test --locked m1_cli_contract::tests`, `scripts/e2e/m1_cli_contract.sh`, and `scripts/faults/m1_cli_contract.sh` pass twice identically. Help and JSON snapshots are complete; all expected exit codes, stderr/stdout boundaries, copy-paste confirmations, token redaction, no-mutation proof, cleanup, and artifact hashes pass `scripts/validate/evidence.sh artifacts/boring-cdc-m1-cli-contract`. Every command owner consumes this registry rather than defining a second envelope.

## Snapshot/action envelope acceptance
Goldens cover fresh/stale/unknown facts, multiple concurrent conditions, blocked and allowed actions, every ownership class, changed action-relevant control revision/fingerprint between dry-run and confirm, unrelated observation progress that leaves authorization valid, expired plans, plan/result causality, redaction, forward-compatible unknown fields/codes, and unique domain owner references. Fixtures prove a stale plan cannot dispatch and every terminal mutation result traces before-snapshot -> plan -> immutable intent/effect -> after-snapshot or explicit safe terminal state.

## Normative evidence tier override: leaf
`evidence_tier=leaf`. This section supersedes the copied generic `Deterministic evidence`, `Checked closure evidence`, and mandatory clean-environment-script wording wherever they require a stronger tier. Required closure evidence is: `cargo fmt --check`, CLI registry/schema validation, `cargo test --locked m1_cli_contract::tests`, parse/help/text/JSON/redaction goldens, and leaf evidence validation. Parse-only process fixtures may run locally, but no PostgreSQL/ClickHouse/Compose, workspace-wide suite, component fault matrix, or second full run is required. All task-specific semantic assertions remain mandatory; only their cheapest valid leaf execution is selected. Component, milestone, and release owners later consume these vectors and run broader suites.


## Approved robustness revision acceptance
Goldens prove unrelated progress and nonce issuance do not stale an action; relevant changes and invalid predicates reject. Exact operation variants resolve to one owner and old command grammar remains compatible. No M2/M5/M6 runtime or measured forecast evidence is required here.

title: Integrate the PostgreSQL capture runtime and feedback loop
description:
Objective / why
Own the missing end-to-end `boring-cdc run` path from CopyBoth receive through bounded spool, atomic SQLite publication/source-state commit, and safe PostgreSQL feedback.

Exact scope
Integrate the M1 decoder with M2 ownership, spool, journal, heartbeat/control routing, startup reconciliation, supervised restart/takeover, requested keepalive replies, and graceful/abrupt shutdown. This task does not implement backfill or destinations.

Traceability only (non-normative)
- docs/PLAN.md §§3–5 and M2
- docs/REQUIREMENTS.md durable-before-ack and capture semantics.

## Embedded canonical contract and unique ownership
Canonical durable-before-feedback integration owner. Own receive→spool→atomic journal→status packet, the typed feedback-permit integration point, requested replies, floor separation, ownership-loss fencing, FailurePolicy/re-arm, graceful shutdown, multi-table journal atomicity and no destination atomicity claim.

## Acceptance Criteria
The structured `acceptance_criteria` field below is normative and must be satisfied in full; this heading exists so tracker lint and human readers find the contract consistently.

## Shared CLI contract consumption
Consume the canonical command registry, help/JSON envelopes, exit codes, stdout/stderr discipline, confirmation rendering, and redaction rules from `boring-cdc-m1-cli-contract`; this Bead owns only its named handler semantics and domain transitions.

## Shared FailurePolicy implementation ownership
Consume the one shared Rust `FailurePolicy` module and persistence adapter from `boring-cdc-m2.1`, bound to `contracts/m0/failure-policy.json`. Own only capture-domain integration: real restart scheduling, retained-WAL/relevant-config re-arm, alive safe-stop, feedback and dispatch gating. ClickHouse and archive handlers integrate the same module under their own later owners.

## Shared policy dependency
Consume the sole shared FailurePolicy core/persistence adapter from `boring-cdc-m2.1`; domain behavior stays here, never a second enum, fingerprint builder or schedule.


## Approved robustness revision ownership
Sole owner of actual safe-stop persist-before-close lifecycle: stop dispatch, persist failed boundary/fingerprint, install run/connection-generation expected-close token, then close. Retain/probe advisory ownership and safe destination draining. Blocking work cannot starve requested feedback/probes; feedback uses only last durable safe boundary.
design:
The runtime acquires both SQLite and deterministic source advisory locks. It parses CopyBoth frames and Origin metadata, spools a bounded whole transaction, atomically commits complete events plus durable source boundary, then sends a standby-status packet whose write/flush/apply positions are all that persisted boundary. It immediately answers requested keepalives without copying `wal_end`. Any advisory-lock or unexpected CopyBoth connection loss fences dispatch and exits; supervised restart/takeover and shutdown reconcile from durable state. In-process advisory-lock reacquire or replication reopen is a test failure.

## Creation-floor hardening
Store the server-established slot-creation consistent point separately from nullable durable transaction-end progress. Never fabricate a source transaction or proactively acknowledge the floor. The M2 integration consumes a typed `FeedbackPermit` decision and tests it with deterministic allow/hold/release stubs; it does not persist importer-gate transitions. Until a later snapshot generation is attached, the no-snapshot permit allows only ordinary durable complete-transaction progress. The persisted snapshot/importer gate and its `open_after_all_import_acks` / `invalidate_and_release` transitions are solely implemented by `boring-cdc-m3-fence`; when attached, requested replies may only use its permitted sentinel/floor/boundary.

## Ownership and command-endpoint hardening
`run` owns a bounded Unix-domain mutating command endpoint and persists idempotent request/result records; status TCP remains read-only. Requests bind a server-issued per-dry-run nonce, ID, run/epoch/config/table-set/anchor/generation fingerprints, nonce-bearing digest/expiry, and peer identity; prior-run nonterminal requests abort after intent reconciliation and never auto-reexecute. Offline mutations acquire both locks and reconcile. The source advisory lock uses a dedicated non-pooled backend PID/nonce plus monotonic ownership deadline; uncertain advisory-lock or unexpected CopyBoth loss fences all dispatch and exits without in-place reacquire/reopen, and supervised successors wait then reconcile.

## Bounded fixed control rows
Both published control relations contain exactly one administration-seeded immutable-key row. The runtime credential has column-limited value UPDATE plus immutable-key-only SELECT; no INSERT, DELETE, key change, or excess column access. Heartbeat/fence updates require exactly one affected row, and each fence uses a unique nonce while SQLite retains history.

## Standalone implementation and evidence contract
Standalone execution contract
This Bead is sufficient for implementation and closure. PLAN/REQUIREMENTS links are navigation only. Preserve the fixed topology: one PostgreSQL source/database/publication/pgoutput slot, one Rust binary and SQLite journal, ClickHouse plus one scheduled JSONL/Parquet archive; durable-before-feedback; destination-independent capture; at-least-once delivery with idempotent convergence; bounded resources; fail-closed unsupported behavior; no cross-epoch version comparison. Values selected by M0 are copied as literals into this Bead or its produced contract before readiness; unresolved/TBD values block readiness.

Inputs, outputs, and ownership
Implement only this Bead's named domain transitions. Consume predecessor artifacts by immutable ID/digest; do not re-own their transitions. State changes use the capture-priority writer and complete SQLite transactions where applicable. External effects require an immutable intent, generation/epoch namespace, reconciliation, and checkpoint advancement only at complete journal transaction boundaries. Every failure names its class, stable fingerprint, failed boundary, allowed actions, and recovery.

Security and observability
Emit redacted JSONL with `schema_version`, monotonically increasing `case_event_seq`, `bead_id`, `scenario_id`, `correlation_id`, `run_id`, `capture_epoch`, `component`, `phase`, `outcome`, `config_fingerprint`, and as applicable `generation`, `intent_id`, `request_id`, XID, commit/end LSN, journal range, anchor/fence, attempt, fault hook, failure class/fingerprint, metric units, and evidence digest. JSON null is used for inapplicable fields. Never log payload values, canonical keys/tuples, snapshot tokens, DSNs, credentials, dry-run nonces, raw driver errors, secret environment names/values, raw source identifiers, or absolute/unapproved paths.

Deterministic evidence
Own comprehensive unit/contract tests for every branch, limit, invalid input, state transition, crash boundary, retry, and stale completion in this Bead. Required commands are `cargo test --locked --workspace --all-targets`, a Bead-specific test filter, `scripts/e2e/m2_capture_runtime.sh`, and `scripts/faults/m2_capture_runtime.sh`. Scripts run from a clean checkout, create isolated volumes/state with fixed seed/profile, build/start pinned Compose services, wait by health conditions rather than sleeps, execute named fault hooks, assert exact state/checkpoint/external effects and metrics, collect evidence, and tear down via a trap. Run twice to prove reproducibility.

Artifacts

Closure records artifact paths/digests and proves log-schema/redaction checks pass.

Integration tests exercise receive -> spool -> journal -> feedback, multi-message transactions, Origin, requested keepalive reply, unexpected CopyBoth-only loss plus supervised restart/takeover, crash before/after journal commit and feedback, heartbeat/control no-op routing, clean shutdown, abrupt termination, oversized input, and two state paths competing for one source advisory lock. Compose restarts indefinitely; the process reads persisted `next_retry_at` and gates transient reconnect with capped backoff/jitter; measured PostgreSQL zombie-backend reap is no greater than takeover. No test path reopens replication or advisory ownership in-process.

Network failures preserve the shared transient schedule across process restart. Deterministic protocol/encoding/limit failures keep the process alive in `capture_safe_stopped`, preserve status and safe destination draining, avoid same-fingerprint replication reconnect, preserve the failed boundary, and never advance feedback. Limit failures re-arm only after startup validates a changed relevant configuration fingerprint and retained WAL; other deterministic failures require confirmed re-seed.

Real JSONL adapter execution belongs to m2-jsonl; real ClickHouse/archive scheduling adapters belong to m4-durability/m5-loops, not this closure. The terminal proof is therefore a direct child of `boring-cdc-v01`; this task barrier remains a milestone child, is blocked by every required leaf task/decision, and blocks the terminal proof through a task-to-task edge. This is the approved non-bypassable closure model. Parent-child links provide hierarchy only and are not treated as completion blockers.

## Milestone evidence manifest

title: Add M2 crash hooks, status JSON, and milestone proof
description:
Objective / why
Make durable boundaries observable and reproducibly fault-injectable.

Exact scope
Hooks around source commit/feedback, bootstrap intent, spool, archive phases, lease/checkpoint/promotion; status/JSON for source/durable/feedback positions, disk, pressure, component state, errors with redaction.

Traceability only (non-normative)
- docs/PLAN.md: §12; §15; §16 M2
- Requirements traceability is retained, but closure uses the embedded contract below.

Dependencies
- boring-cdc-m2-heartbeat
- boring-cdc-m2-reconcile
- boring-cdc-m2-pressure
- boring-cdc-m2-jsonl
- boring-cdc-m2-init-recovery

## Failure telemetry ownership
Expose stable processing failure class/fingerprint, first/last failure, attempts/next retry, failed XID/final LSN or journal range, observed transaction bytes/events versus limits, retry-armed state, and WAL-headroom consequence with redaction.

## Embedded canonical contract and unique ownership
Own `scripts/acceptance/m2.sh` and `scripts/faults/m2_matrix.sh`, every commit/feedback/spool/ownership/archive/checkpoint hook, status/JSON freshness, heartbeat→real JSONL no-op, nested driver-error redaction and machine-readable artifact index.

## Command ownership
Own public `boring-cdc status [--json]`; both render the same fresh derived conditions and redacted evidence, and neither exposes mutation.

## Acceptance Criteria
The structured `acceptance_criteria` field below is normative and must be satisfied in full; this heading exists so tracker lint and human readers find the contract consistently.

## Shared CLI contract consumption
Consume the canonical command registry, help/JSON envelopes, exit codes, stdout/stderr discipline, confirmation rendering, and redaction rules from `boring-cdc-m1-cli-contract`; this Bead owns only its named handler semantics and domain transitions.

## Canonical SystemSnapshot projection
Own the fresh runtime projection of the shared `SystemSnapshot` envelope. Join domain facts without copying ownership: source/durable/feedback boundaries, ownership, budgets, destinations/checkpoints/generations/audits, concurrent conditions, evidence/runbook IDs, blockers, allowed actions, and safe next-command templates. Persist causal before-plan-after postcondition evidence for owner-executed actions; never infer success from logs or add an independent status transition machine.

## Canonical M2 condition ownership
This Bead is the sole declaration/projection owner for the condition IDs first available in M2: `healthy`, `degraded`, `destination_blocked` (generic destination condition; later adapters add owned reason evidence), `schema_blocked`, `capture_safe_stopped`, `slot_invalid_requires_reseed`, `journal_corrupt_requires_reseed`, `publication_drift_requires_reseed`, `bootstrap_ambiguous_requires_restart`, `heartbeat_degraded`, `promotion_recovery_required`, `source_identity_blocked`, `ownership_lost`, and `unsafe_durability`. It authors exactly these `COND-*` declaration rows. M3 owns the first declarations for backfill/snapshot/reseed conditions; M4 owns `clickhouse_durability_unverified`; M6 consumes all rows and owns only cross-domain composition, severity, freshness, and hysteresis.

## Series evidence handoff
Retain redacted originating prompts, first implementation output, observed failures, human corrections and exact code/scenario/command digests under this milestone evidence root. docs/SERIES_EXECUTION.md maps consumers. Do not claim later destination/anchor/promotion behavior at this milestone; content uses these immutable artifacts rather than reconstructing history or adding new product acceptance.


## Approved robustness revision ownership
Integrate real m2-schema writer attestation, m2-journal scheduler, m2-pressure pin/checkpoint progress and m2-ownership action predicates. Project domain-owned control revisions and expected-close state without reimplementing them.
design:
Implementation / decision notes
Fault hooks are test-only or explicit local experiment controls and cannot expose secrets.

Preserve these global invariants: one PostgreSQL source, one publication, one pgoutput slot, one Rust binary, one SQLite journal, ClickHouse plus one JSONL/Parquet archive; durable-before-feedback; destination-independent capture; at-least-once/idempotent convergence; explicit bounded failure; no comparison of source versions across capture epochs.

## Accepted review corrections
Own implemented status/JSON/metrics listener exposure: loopback/Unix default and authenticated TLS for explicit non-loopback, plus overall_health and concurrent conditions.

## Ownership and command-endpoint hardening
`run` owns a bounded Unix-domain mutating command endpoint and persists idempotent request/result records; status TCP remains read-only. Requests bind a server-issued per-dry-run nonce, ID, run/epoch/config/table-set/anchor/generation fingerprints, nonce-bearing digest/expiry, and peer identity; prior-run nonterminal requests abort after intent reconciliation and never auto-reexecute. Offline mutations acquire both locks and reconcile. The source advisory lock uses a dedicated non-pooled backend PID/nonce plus monotonic ownership deadline; uncertain advisory-lock or unexpected CopyBoth loss fences all dispatch and exits without in-place reacquire/reopen, and supervised successors wait then reconcile.

## Standalone implementation and evidence contract
Standalone execution contract
This Bead is sufficient for implementation and closure. PLAN/REQUIREMENTS links are navigation only. Preserve the fixed topology: one PostgreSQL source/database/publication/pgoutput slot, one Rust binary and SQLite journal, ClickHouse plus one scheduled JSONL/Parquet archive; durable-before-feedback; destination-independent capture; at-least-once delivery with idempotent convergence; bounded resources; fail-closed unsupported behavior; no cross-epoch version comparison. Values selected by M0 are copied as literals into this Bead or its produced contract before readiness; unresolved/TBD values block readiness.

Inputs, outputs, and ownership
Implement only this Bead's named domain transitions. Consume predecessor artifacts by immutable ID/digest; do not re-own their transitions. State changes use the capture-priority writer and complete SQLite transactions where applicable. External effects require an immutable intent, generation/epoch namespace, reconciliation, and checkpoint advancement only at complete journal transaction boundaries. Every failure names its class, stable fingerprint, failed boundary, allowed actions, and recovery.

Security and observability
Emit redacted JSONL with `schema_version`, monotonically increasing `case_event_seq`, `bead_id`, `scenario_id`, `correlation_id`, `run_id`, `capture_epoch`, `component`, `phase`, `outcome`, `config_fingerprint`, and as applicable `generation`, `intent_id`, `request_id`, XID, commit/end LSN, journal range, anchor/fence, attempt, fault hook, failure class/fingerprint, metric units, and evidence digest. JSON null is used for inapplicable fields. Never log payload values, canonical keys/tuples, snapshot tokens, DSNs, credentials, dry-run nonces, raw driver errors, secret environment names/values, raw source identifiers, or absolute/unapproved paths.

Deterministic evidence
Own comprehensive unit/contract tests for every branch, limit, invalid input, state transition, crash boundary, retry, and stale completion in this Bead. Required commands are `cargo test --locked --workspace --all-targets`, a Bead-specific test filter, `scripts/e2e/m2_fault_status.sh`, and `scripts/faults/m2_fault_status.sh`. Scripts run from a clean checkout, create isolated volumes/state with fixed seed/profile, build/start pinned Compose services, wait by health conditions rather than sleeps, execute named fault hooks, assert exact state/checkpoint/external effects and metrics, collect evidence, and tear down via a trap. Run twice to prove reproducibility.

Artifacts
Write `artifacts/boring-cdc-m2-fault-status/<scenario_id>/<seed>/` containing `manifest.json`, `commands.txt`, `versions.json`, redacted `config.json`, `logs/boring-cdc.jsonl`, `state/before.json`, `state/after.json`, `fault-timeline.json`, oracle/packet evidence when applicable, stdout/stderr, and SHA-256 inventory. `manifest.json` records schema version, Bead/case, git and binary hashes, image digests, seed/profile, exact commands/exit codes, configuration and source/table fingerprints, assertions, artifact hashes, outcome, and failure fingerprint. Closure records artifact paths/digests and proves log-schema/redaction checks pass.

## Snapshot revision and causality
Derive observation state_revision/snapshot_id from canonical persisted provenance and source digests; project the separate domain control revisions, never increment/re-own their semantics here. m2-schema persists revisions and domain transitions advance them atomically; m2-ownership owns action-specific validation. It consumes compatible leaf/component claims by digest and reruns any invalidated prerequisite; it does not run later endurance/release matrices.

Consume real M2 capture, shared-policy, spool, reconciliation and JSONL evidence only. Compound creation-floor/slot-invalid/WAL-unavailable rejection and the actual live-process suppression/config-rearm/retained-WAL/feedback integration are required here. Earlier spool/core policy fixtures use explicit runtime doubles; this terminal proves real capture integration. Actual ClickHouse and full archive adapter/selector evidence remains owned by M4/M5 and cannot be required or claimed at M2 closure. Preserve contract digests and independent boundary provenance.


## Approved robustness revision acceptance
Busy-runtime confirmation survives unrelated source/checkpoint/telemetry progress and nonce issuance; changed control revisions/history/reserves fail. Saturation/slow-storage checks prove real failure/control/checkpoint/GC progress plus capture probes/feedback. Stalled reader and fresh/stale actual-writer evidence are visible; deterministic safe-stop versus ownership-loss races run via same-code harness and real M2 adapters.

## Embedded JSONL segment commit skeleton

2. Retry exactly that intent range after failure; never silently widen it because newer events arrived.

description:
Objective / why
Block unsafe source/local contradictions and corrupted/missing journal ranges before streaming.

Exact scope
Durably load/update `source_state` and execute slot/source/timeline/publication/protocol startup comparison; run quick/integrity checks, event/transaction checksums, sequence/count/checkpoint-range validation, replay-floor and spool scans; persist exact blocked/reseed/state transitions before streaming.

Each reports integrity/source reconciliation, replay floor/ranges, nonterminal bootstrap/promotion/reseed intents, and exact blocked/recovery state without loading administration credentials or mutating checkpoints.

## Persisted intent ownership
Own startup/recovery classification of every nonterminal command, bootstrap, promotion, and re-seed intent, including `prepared` plus existing slot without persisted floor/token -> `bootstrap_ambiguous_requires_restart`. M1 preflight remains stateless.

## Embedded canonical contract and unique ownership
Own top-to-bottom startup outcomes, creation-floor special cases, quick/full integrity, checkpoint/range/schema checks, prior-run abort ordering, failure schedule restoration, archive intent reconciliation and local stub external-ahead block; no M4/M5 evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria
The structured `acceptance_criteria` field below is normative and must be satisfied in full; this heading exists so tracker lint and human readers find the contract consistently.

## Embedded startup reconciliation protocol
### 4.3 Source identity and capture epochs

Persist in `source_state`:

- `capture_epoch`;
- PostgreSQL system identifier and timeline;
- database identity;
- slot name and plugin;
- publication-definition fingerprint;
- supported-protocol configuration fingerprint;
- last received LSN;
- nullable durable transaction end LSN derived only from a decoded, durably published source transaction;
- nullable server-established slot-creation floor LSN, stored separately from transaction progress and valid only for its matching nonterminal bootstrap intent;
- last feedback LSN, including whether a requested bootstrap reply merely repeated the verified creation floor; and
- observed server slot positions and status.

Include `capture_epoch` in transaction and event identities. Never compare `source_version` values across capture epochs.

On every startup, reconcile the live source with local state before streaming. Rows are evaluated top-to-bottom and the first match wins:

| Condition | Required behavior |
|---|---|
| Source, timeline, database, slot/plugin, publication, or protocol fingerprint mismatch | Block startup and require inspection/re-seed as appropriate |
| Bootstrap intent is `prepared`, the slot exists, and no creation floor/snapshot token was persisted | Transition to `bootstrap_ambiguous_requires_restart`; section 7.1 provenance and WAL-continuity recovery takes precedence over generic ahead-of-local handling |
| Matching nonterminal bootstrap has a persisted creation floor, no local source transaction exists, the slot is valid and required resume WAL is available, and server `confirmed_flush_lsn` is null or equals that floor | Treat it only as the server-established creation floor; request the pinned protocol zero sentinel or repeat that persisted floor only, and never populate durable transaction progress from it |
| Server `confirmed_flush_lsn` ahead of both the verified creation floor and SQLite durable transaction end, outside the preceding ambiguous-bootstrap case | `requires_reseed`; local restored state may have lost acknowledged events |
| Required local resume LSN no longer available or slot invalid | `requires_reseed` |
| Server slot behind local durable transaction end LSN and resume WAL remains available | Request the local durable position; tolerate deterministic duplicate delivery |
| Server and local positions compatible | Request SQLite's durable transaction end LSN; test PostgreSQL's effective restart rule `max(requested_lsn, confirmed_flush_lsn)` |

Server-confirmed progress may advance only through a durably committed published transaction end LSN. The slot-creation `consistent_point` is not a decoded transaction, is never copied into `durable_transaction_end_lsn`, and is never proactively acknowledged. Before the first journaled source transaction, a requested status reply uses the pinned protocol's zero sentinel or repeats only the verified server-established creation floor; it cannot manufacture progress. After durable transaction progress exists, a standby-status update sets `write_lsn`, `flush_lsn`, and `apply_lsn` to that same persisted safe boundary. It includes the current client timestamp and requested-reply flag required by the pinned protocol. A keepalive with `replyRequested=1` triggers an immediate status packet even when the safe boundary has not advanced, but never copies informational keepalive `wal_end`, the merely received WAL end, a timer-derived position, or a destination checkpoint. Startup fixtures cover null/equal creation-floor representations, requested positions on both sides of `confirmed_flush_lsn`, requested keepalive replies, and PostgreSQL's effective `max(requested_lsn, confirmed_flush_lsn)` behavior.

## Approved robustness revision ownership

`bootstrap_anchors` contains at least:

```text
anchor_id
capture_epoch
generation
lower_stitch_lsn
start_seq
snapshot_boundary_lsn
snapshot_complete_seq
post_copy_fence_nonce
post_copy_fence_lsn
post_copy_fence_seq
table_set_fingerprint
snapshot_schema_fingerprints
state
expires_at
```

A usable anchor represents a complete baseline plus every required concurrent journal event from its lower complete boundary through a post-copy durable capture fence. For initial bootstrap, `(snapshot_boundary_lsn, start_seq)` is the slot `(consistent_point, current complete journal boundary)` persisted before copying; for an existing slot, `(lower_stitch_lsn, start_seq)` is the last locally durable complete source boundary persisted before exporting a snapshot. `post_copy_fence_seq` is the complete journal position atomically paired with the published control-row fence's `post_copy_fence_lsn` and nonce. Anchor state can transition to `complete` only when all valid snapshot chunks, schema bindings/import acknowledgements, the lower proof, and that matching durable capture-fence record exist. Retention pins `start_seq`. An arbitrary retained sequence, an invalidated generation, or snapshot completion without the fence is never advertised as a valid empty-destination bootstrap point.

Important constraints:

- unique `(capture_epoch, source/slot identity, transaction end LSN)`;
- unique positional connector event ID; an existing identity with a different stored payload hash is corruption, not a second event;
- monotonic journal sequence;
- source durable LSN changes in the same transaction as its event publication;
- bootstrap intent/import transitions are monotonic and make exporter loss or ambiguous remote slot creation visible;
- durable capture fences and heartbeat control events reference a capture epoch, source transaction, and complete journal sequence; materializers route them as internal transaction-preserving no-ops;
- destination checkpoint references a complete committed journal transaction boundary plus `capture_epoch`, anchor identity where applicable, configuration fingerprint, generation, and nullable `current_failure_id`; retry schedules/reasons exist only in `processing_failures`;
- runtime ownership records the `run_id`, dedicated advisory-lock backend PID/nonce, monotonic ownership deadline, loss state, and takeover/reconciliation evidence;
- operator command request IDs are unique per server-issued dry-run nonce; the persisted nonce, canonical payload/digest, run ID, state, and result make one dry-run's lost-response retries idempotent, while same-ID/different-payload reuse blocks and every nonterminal prior-run request becomes `aborted_by_restart` after remote-intent reconciliation;

- archive segment intent is immutable once selected;
- immutable transaction and event payload checksums;
- immutable relation schemas by fingerprint; and
